per_shot.note: Real hab: ribbed ceiling with fixtures, riveted panels, plated floor; arc lamp pools warm on wall/floor; star chart, books, console read; lower third of frame is a large near-black floor expanse and the rug/radio are cropped at the edge.
Fern reads instantly, radio has a lit amber dial and antenna, rug shows a woven diamond pattern with fringe; desk lamp and porthole add warmth; desk-top clutter is small and murky.
Rug pattern and fringe are clear and handsome, books on bracket shelf read as books, console screen glows; dusk from portholes does not visibly spill onto the floor.

Star chart framed with brass corners, arc lamp casts a warm cone and pool; specimen jars read; lamp light cone is a hard-edged wedge rather than a soft bloom, fridge is the brightest flat object and competes with the suit.
Kettle, cups, tea towel and tiled splashback read as a galley; bunk has duvet, pillow and folded book; pinboard and wall sconce feel lived-in; bunk sits in shadow with only a small sconce pool.
Distinct cool slate room with teal trim and cool ceiling light, arc lamp still warm; reads clearly as a different mood but drifts colder than the sanctuary brief wants.
Warm dusty-rose walls with deep red wainscot and pink-tinted fixtures; the most distinct and inviting alt palette.
Olive-green walls with timber wainscot and brass trim; distinct and pleasant but the green-yellow ceiling light flattens it toward murky.

top_issues.why: At play scale the bottom ~35% of frame is near-black plating with no light landing on it, so the furnished room occupies a thin band and reads smaller and less rich than the close-ups.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let porthole dusk and the ceiling fixtures throw soft pools onto the near floor, or add a low foreground element (runner, floor grate glow) so the lower frame carries warm value rather than void.

top_issues.issue: Palettes change walls but little else
top_issues.why: Wall hue, trim and fixture tint change, but floor, ceiling material and furnishings stay identical, so the palettes are good but edge toward recolours rather than rooms with their own mood.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each palette one signature material change (floor tone, ceiling panel finish, trim metal) and tune fixture colour so SLATEBED stays cosy rather than clinical and VERDANT avoids the muddy yellow-green cast.

top_issues.issue: Arc lamp cone is a hard geometric wedge
top_issues.why: The beam reads as a flat translucent triangle with crisp edges instead of light blooming softly into the air and landing on the wall.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Feather the cone's edges and fade it with distance so it reads as glow plus a pool on wall and floor.

top_issues.issue: Small items lose detail at play scale
top_issues.why: Books, jars and the radio dial are tiny in the mid shot; the radio is clipped at the left edge, so a fully furnished room does not show off its purchases at gameplay size.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Slightly enlarge or add rim light / a local practical to the bookshelf and radio so they read from the gameplay camera.

top_issues.why: The cream fridge is the largest bright surface in frame and pulls the eye near the white suit.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop its value a step or put it partly in shadow so the suit stays the most legible thing in frame.

protect: Ribbed ceiling with recessed fixtures, riveted wall panels and plated floor: the room is no longer a box

Fern reads, but the radio is a black box with a dot, the desk is an untextured slab, rug has no pattern, ceiling is pure black.
Books read; console is a grey block with a teal strip; rug is a flat orange plane; walls single flat colour.
Star chart reads; floor lamp casts almost no pool; fridge and table are flat-shaded boxes.
Galley is a green box with cylinders (no kettle), bunk is a slab with a red block (no bedding), pinboard is three flat squares.
Grey-green flat walls with green trim; same box, a recolour of one surface.

top_issues.issue: Room is a flat box with a black ceiling
top_issues.why: No panels, ribs, conduit, floor plating or ceiling fixtures; exactly the 'basic' room the brief calls out.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build ceiling structure with fixtures, panel seams and plated floor with value variation across surfaces.

top_issues.issue: Furnishings do not read as themselves
top_issues.why: Rug has no weave, radio has no glowing dial, bunk has no bedding, galley has no kettle; purchases look like placeholder blocks.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each item its identifying detail: rug pattern and fringe, lit radio dial, pillow and duvet, kettle with spout and handle.

top_issues.why: Floor lamp and portholes cast no visible pools; the only light pool is the suit's own.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add warm pools from the lamp and practicals on wall and floor, and dusk spill from portholes.

top_issues.why: Only wall hue and trim change; nothing about materials or light gives each room a mood.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Vary materials, trim and light colour per palette so each is a distinct room.

protect: Star chart and coloured book spines

why: A delivers a structured, warmly lit hab where every bought item reads with its identifying detail and palettes feel like distinct rooms; B is the flat placeholder box with blocky furnishings and recolour-only palettes.
